"Satisfy is a full-dive VRMMO developed by the S.A. Group and regulated by the supercomputer Morpheus. It has a player base exceeding 2 billion, runs on ultra-realistic AI for NPCs (making them nearly indistinguishable from players except by green name tags for ordinary NPCs), and emphasizes player-driven world development with minimal developer intervention. Time flows at a 3:1 ratio (1 real-world hour ≈ 3 in-game hours). Sessions last up to 20 hours, after which players are forced offline for 6 hours. There is no customer service center; the world evolves through player actions, NPC interactions, and information exchange.⁠Overgeared.fandom

The world is vast (West Continent alone larger than Earth), with continents, seas, kingdoms, empires, dungeons, fields, and later divine/mythic dimensions. Players log in via capsules. Character creation has limited customization (appearance close to real life with options for skin, hair, eyes, tattoos, weight, but height/skeletal structure largely fixed). Originally human-only; non-human races require hidden quests or special conditions.⁠Overgeared.fandom

Core Mechanics
Death and penalties: Beginners under level 10 lose no experience on death (quest failure still penalizes). Dying twice within 24 hours locks the account for 12 hours. Timed quests cannot be safely exited. Killed entities fade into grey light.
Stun: Taking ≥40% health in one hit stuns the character.
Weight and inventory: Exceeding weight limit slows movement proportionally (e.g., 200% excess halves speed and risks “weakened” state). Warehouses exist in communities (registration + password; summonable via magic; small fees to open/store).
Travel: Walking, mounts, carriages (base 5 gold in safe zones; higher in dangerous areas for risk), and later teleportation or dimensional travel. Carriages help cross monster areas safely.
Parties: Up to 24 members (players or NPCs). Leader sets loot rules (e.g., leader distribution, need/greed). Shared affinity changes and some buffs. Useful for raids and hunting.
Currency: Gold, silver, bronze (roughly 1 gold = 100 silver). Auction house commissions scale with item rating (higher for rarer items). Real-money conversion exists and is significant (e.g., early values around 100 gold ≈ substantial real currency).
Control and movement: Full-body realism. Characters respond to player intent like a real body, modified by system correction, stats, terrain, and skills. “Control” refers to skillful prediction, positioning, timing, weak-point targeting, evasion of non-targeted attacks, blocking, countering, and efficient skill use. Terrain matters (e.g., heavy boots in desert sink into sand). Combat is action-oriented rather than pure tab-targeting.
Stats: Core stats include Strength (attack power, health, weight limit; effects awaken/improve every 100 levels), Stamina, Agility, Intelligence (magic power/mana), plus class-specific ones like Dexterity (production). Players get 10 fixed stat points per level; NPCs get variable (6–20). Named NPCs have superior base capabilities and much higher effective health.
Classes: Over 120,000 possible. Ratings: Normal (common, white font), Rare, Epic, Unique, Legendary, Myth (and growth types or “Only One”). Hidden classes (Rare+) are special. Types: combat (easy leveling via monsters), production (raise stats via crafting/selling; often have Dexterity), and others. Advancements every 100 levels unlock more skills/potential. Legendary classes (very few) grant major privileges like wearing restricted gear (with penalties until understanding is gained) and control immunity.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Items and ratings: Same rating scale (Normal → Myth). Equipment has slots, visible appearance, durability (needs repair), and usage conditions (level/stats/class—Legendary classes often ignore these with penalties). Enhancement up to +10 using stones; success chance drops with higher enhancement and rating. Success = +1; failure = –3. Higher enhancements add auras/lights (blue at +6, deeper colors later, white at +9). Options, creator signatures (especially high-grade), and understanding systems exist. Production methods, blueprints, and materials heavily influence outcome.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Other systems: Quests (ratings, timed, failure penalties), titles, skills (with cooldowns, grades), pets (taming expanded later), affinity with NPCs (shared in parties; high affinity unlocks stories/growth), reputation. Later “First Update” added Spiritual Energy/cultivation ranks, Treasures (no usage restrictions but resource costs; risky crafting), expanded pet taming, etc.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Crafting / Production Systems
Production classes (especially blacksmiths) are central. Most blacksmiths use an automated system: select design/production method, register materials, start process (hammering auto-runs; 5 min–several hours). Better materials raise rating chances. Manual labor (physically hammering) increases odds of higher ratings and options and is favored by rankers.⁠Novgo

Factors affecting quality: skill level, materials, time, tools (hammers with bonuses), dexterity, understanding of items (disassemble/repair/use to raise understanding → eventually learn recipes and reduce equip penalties), and special skills. Legendary blacksmithing (e.g., Pagma’s Successor path) masters basic skills, opens advanced ones (creation, appraisal, repair, disassemble, etc.), allows designing new production methods, raises chances for Rare/Epic/Unique/Legendary outputs, permanently boosts stats/reputation on high-tier crafts, and lets the creator’s name appear on items. High-grade crafted gear can have extended safe enhancement ranges or signature prestige.⁠Anilore

Smithies/forges are workplaces. Minerals, ores, special materials (scales, metals from specific regions/dimensions), and later Treasures expand options. Crafting drives economy, player reputation, guild power, and plot—high-end gear is social and political currency.

The World and Places
West Continent is the primary starting area: massive, populated by billions, home to numerous kingdoms and the former Saharan Empire (later integrated into the Overgeared Empire). Separated from the East Continent by the Red Sea. Diverse climates—northern cold/snowfields, deserts, mountains, forests, canyons, swamps, plains.⁠Overgeared.fandom

Key locations (vividly):

Reinhardt: Former capital of Eternal Kingdom, later capital of Overgeared Kingdom/Empire. Bustling political, military, and industrial hub with temples, smithies, academies, fortifications, and expanding infrastructure. Grows into a center of power with divine elements later.
Winston: Large northern city, early hub for Grid. Home to Khan’s famous smithy. Busy streets, commercial districts, noble presence (Steim family influence), and surrounding threats from churches or monsters.
Reidan: Once a declining desert/arid territory granted as a duchy. Harsh sands, limited water, sparse population initially. Transformed into an industrial powerhouse and supply center through farming innovations, mining, and development. Features mountains (Dravian), fields, and strategic value.
Bairan: Smaller village near Winston that becomes a guild base. More rural, with smithing and adventuring opportunities.
Patrian: Major fortress city, militaristic atmosphere, frequent early player activity.
Titan: Former Saharan capital, chosen for its unique black mithril mine. Imperial grandeur—palaces, legions, economic power.
Galest: Largest port city of the former empire, gateway to the Red Sea, economic artery with ships, trade, and coastal vibrancy.
Other notable areas: Kesan Canyon (steep, dangerous walls; hermit hideouts), Dravian Mountains (former dragon nest, monster-infested), northern snowfields (Frost Orcs, harsh cold), Cokro Island Dungeon (multi-floor with periodic boss Hell Gao), various temples (Yatan Church sites of dark rituals, Rebecca Church holy sites), fields/plains for hunting, and later Overgeared World (mythic divine dimension tied to gods and temples in Reinhardt, granting special effects).
East Continent features different kingdoms (Hwan, Cho, Kaya, etc.) with distinct cultures, martial/spiritual elements, and access challenges. Hell, divine realms, Abyss (between dimensions/servers), and other planes appear later. Servers function as “dimensions” with unique resources, bosses, and travel costs/limits via the Abyss.⁠Invenglobal

Kingdoms/Empires include Eternal (northern, later conquered), Saharan (vast imperial power with Red Knights, later declined/integrated), Gauss, Fold, Siren (aquatic elements), Valhalla, and many others (some destroyed or vassalized). Politics involve nobility, churches (Rebecca vs. Yatan), guilds, and player kingdoms.

Major NPCs
There are thousands of NPCs; exhaustive coverage of every minor one is impossible. Named/super-named NPCs have gold names, infinite growth potential, high health, story impact, and superior capabilities. Semi-named can break limits with training. Ordinary NPCs have green names and stat caps. High affinity unlocks depth, quests, and growth. Treating them as real people yields strong results.⁠Overgeared.fandom

Key named NPCs (descriptions based on established lore):

Khan: Elderly, pot-bellied blacksmith craftsman of Winston, descendant of Albatino (first human craftsman). Proud family tradition of excellence. Firm-willed, initially pressured by corrupt companies. Becomes Grid’s teacher, friend, and father figure; later Chief of Reinhardt’s smithy and rises to Legendary Blacksmith. Completes masterwork pieces even near death. Deep loyalty and insight.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Irene (Irene Winston von Steim): Beautiful noblewoman with silver hair, clear blue eyes, and elegant oval face. Only daughter/successor of Earl (later Duke) Steim. Kidnapped by Yatan Church and rescued; later marries Grid, becomes lady of Winston, queen/empress figure. Dutiful, status-aware but not arrogant; develops cooking/baking hobbies to please Grid. Loyal knights; mother to Lord.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Piaro: Former Captain of Saharan Empire’s Red Knights, Legendary Farmer, and Great Swordsman. Initially a ragged, matted-haired hermit in Kesan Canyon seeking revenge (sickness of the heart). Becomes Grid’s duke, general, and agricultural backbone. Wears straw hat and farming tools; turns farming tools and everyday objects into devastating weapons via qi. Married to elf Beniyaru; has daughter. Loyal, grows into a mythic-tinged powerhouse.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Braham (Braham Eshwald): Direct descendant vampire (child of Beriache), Legendary Great Magician, Duke of Wisdom. Transcendently beautiful—pale skin, blood-red eyes, sharp fangs; appearance causes strong reactions. Arrogant, views most as fools, pursues ultimate knowledge/magic. Complex history of experiments, regrets (Mumud), grudges (Pagma, Marie Rose). High affinity leads to deep alliance with Grid; later divine aspects.⁠Overgeared.fandom
Asmophel: Former Red Knight colleague of Piaro. Complex past involving brainwashing/drugs and crimes; seeks atonement. Loyal subordinate and commander under Grid; skilled knight.
Mercedes: Legendary Knight, top Saharan talent, later high-ranking Overgeared figure (commander). Extremely capable in combat and negotiations.
Lord Steim: Son of Grid and Irene; prodigious young noble with strong potential and protection details.
Jude: Semi-named/Grade A knight under Grid; high combat stats, loyal, grows significantly.
Minor: Semi-named miner/metals detector; unique skills, breaks limits through development.
Rabbit: Administrator/merchant type; economic expertise for the kingdom.
Kasim: Assassin (later Lantier path); protects Lord and leads shadows.
Sticks: Elven Great Sage; knowledge and support.
Others of note: Earl/Marquis Ashur (powerful magician, complex relations), Bland (magic swordsman turned farmer enthusiast), Smith (blacksmith who grows under Grid’s influence), various blacksmiths (White, Enoch, etc.), church figures (Isabel of Rebecca), emperors/princes of Saharan (Juander, etc.), and many more (Noll the vampire, Ke’ong the dwarf, etc.). Super-named include legends and major world influencers.
NPCs drive stories, provide quests, grow with or against players, and form the living backbone of the world. Affinity, training, and genuine interaction are key to unlocking their full potential.

This captures the core systems, geography, and prominent NPCs of Satisfy’s worldview as detailed across the novel, wiki, and related sources. The setting prioritizes realism, player agency, crafting depth, and emergent politics over pure combat. Create all of it in a way the player can play it in a computer with mouse and keyboard or in the mobile phone.         
**Satisfy has over 120,000 possible classes.** Most are Normal-rated (common, publicly known, white font text). Higher ratings (Rare, Epic, Unique, Legendary, Myth, and some Unrated/Growth-type) are **Hidden Classes**. Classes advance every 100 levels (1st Advancement at 100, 2nd at 200, etc.), unlocking more skills and potential. Normal classes often have the highest long-term potential per advancement, while Hidden Classes start stronger and more unique but can be more restricted.[](<https://overgeared.fandom.com/wiki/Classes>)

Classes fall into broad types: **Combat**, **Production**, and **Other/Non-combat**. Players can hold multiple classes in some cases (especially later or with special conditions). Many classes have growth versions that can rise in rating through achievements.

### The Nine Original Legendary Classes
These are based on the nine previous Legends of Satisfy’s history. Obtaining one typically resets level/stats/skills to 1 (or lower) and is extremely rare (often one active user at a time for the pure versions). They carry major privileges (e.g., control immunity, gear flexibility with penalties until understanding is gained).

| Legendary Class                  | Based On          | Focus                          | Known User(s) / Notes                  |
|----------------------------------|-------------------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Pagma’s Successor (Legendary Blacksmith) | Pagma            | Blacksmithing + Swordsmanship | Grid (primary example)                |
| Sword Saint                      | Muller           | Ultimate swordsmanship        | Kraugel                               |
| Legendary Great Magician         | Braham           | Magic / Wisdom                | Grid (partial/additional), Braham (NPC) |
| Demon Slayer                     | Alex             | Anti-demon / Gunner elements  | Yura                                  |
| Legendary Assassin (Lantier)     | Lantier          | Assassination                 | Faker                                 |
| Legendary Archer (Bow Saint / Povia’s Successor) | Povia     | Archery                       | Jishuka                               |
| Undefeated King’s Successor      | Madra            | General / Strategy / Combat   | Oasis (attempted/failed in some accounts) |
| Legendary Tailor (Kruger’s)      | Kruger           | Tailoring / Debuffing         | Unclaimed or limited info             |
| Legendary Miner (Gis’s)          | Gis              | Mining / Tanking              | Unclaimed or limited info             |

Other Legendary or near-Legendary examples that appear or are referenced:
- Legendary Farmer (Piaro – creation skill: Farming Method Creation)
- Legendary Martial Artist
- Legendary Painter
- Legendary Scientist
- Legendary Spearman
- Legendary Explorer (Skunk)
- Guardian of Light (defensive/light reflection – associated with Vantner later)
- Baal’s Contractor (Agnus – growth/special)
- Saintess (Ruby)
- Mumud’s Successor (Euphemina – started as Duplicator, growth-type Legendary)
- Magic Swordsman of the Epics (Grid-related growth path)
- Dungeon Maker (Eat Spicy Jokbal)
- War King (Ares)
- Aura Master (Hurent)
- And various others that reach or approach Legendary through growth.[](<https://www.reddit.com/r/Overgeared/comments/l05lmq/legendary_classes_spoilers/>)

### Notable Classes That Appear in the Story
**Production-focused**
- Blacksmith (Normal → various advancements; Legendary version via Pagma)
- Alchemist (often secondary)
- Tailor
- Miner
- Farmer (Legendary version exists)
- Chef / related production
- Painter, Scientist (Legendary versions mentioned)

**Combat-focused**
- Warrior / Swordsman (many variants)
- Knight
- Martial Artist → possible Asura advancement (Regas)
- Spearman / Magic Spearman / Legendary Spearman
- Archer / Bow-related
- Assassin → Master of Swiftness / Hidden Sword / Lantier path (Faker)
- Magician variants: Fire Magician, Ice Mystic, Explosion Sorcerer, Illusionist, Mixed Magician, etc.
- Necromancer
- Magic Swordsman
- Lightning Swordsman
- Qigong Master
- Orator (support/buff – Huroi)
- Duplicator (Euphemina’s early class – copies skills)

**Other / Hybrid / Special**
- Saintess (holy/healing)
- Demon-related (Demon Slayer, Demon World Noble, etc.)
- Death God / soul-related
- Pet-related or tamer variants
- Explorer
- Various knight/commander or noble-linked classes
- Skeleton/undead variants (for certain summons or special characters)

Many more appear briefly: Debirion’s Envoy, Impregnable Fortress, Quick Draw Swordsman, Monster Discerner, Prince (Lord), and dozens of named or minimal-info classes listed on the wiki (the fandom currently tracks around 151 mentioned classes).[](<https://overgeared.fandom.com/wiki/Category:Classes>)

### Possibilities Not Fully Shown or Only Hinted
Because there are 120,000+ classes, the vast majority never appear on-screen. The system is designed for discovery:
- Extremely specialized Normal classes for every craft, combat style, support role, or lifestyle (e.g., obscure mineral specialists, specific elemental hybrids, vehicle/pilot types, social/political classes, etc.).
- Countless Rare/Epic/Unique Hidden Classes tied to specific quests, regions, NPCs, gods, monsters, or achievements.
- Growth-type classes that start lower and can climb all the way to Legendary or Myth.
- Myth-rated classes (opened as a possibility through major world events and Grid’s achievements).
- Multi-class combinations and third/fourth classes for high-level or special users.
- Race-linked classes (after non-human options unlock via hidden quests).
- Divine, demonic, cultivator/Spiritual Energy classes (post-First Update), Treasure-related, or dimension-specific classes.
- Completely unique “Only One” style classes.
- Failed or incomplete Legendary paths (e.g., some Undefeated King attempts).
- NPC-only or semi-exclusive classes that players can later access under rare conditions.

In short: every major combat role, production profession, support function, and hybrid you can imagine exists in some form, plus thousands of highly specific or story-unique variants. The story only shows a tiny fraction—mostly those relevant to Grid, the Overgeared members, top rankers, and major NPCs. New classes continue to be discoverable through exploration, quests, and world changes.

**Satisfy’s world** is vast and multi-layered. The primary playable area is the **Human World**, which contains the **West Continent** and **East Continent**, separated by the **Red Sea** (also called the Dead Sea in some contexts). Beyond these lie other planes: **Hell**, **Asgard** (divine realm), the **Overgeared World** (later mythic dimension), elemental worlds, cultivation-related spaces, the Abyss between dimensions/servers, and more. The West Continent alone is larger than Earth, with a population in the billions. No complete official map exists in-universe for players at the start; exploration is key.[](<https://overgeared.fandom.com/wiki/West_Continent>)

Descriptions below focus on places that receive meaningful attention or description in the novel. Minor mentions (single-line villages, unnamed fields, etc.) are summarized or omitted for practicality, as there are hundreds.

### Continents and Major Realms
- **West Continent**: The main setting for most of the story. Medieval Western European-inspired fantasy with kingdoms, empires, deserts, mountains, forests, snowfields, volcanoes, and seas. Diverse climates: cold north (snowfields around Winston), arid west (Reidan desert region), central fertile/plains areas, volcanic zones, and coastal regions. Home to the Saharan Empire (later integrated) and numerous kingdoms. Larger than Earth.[](<https://overgeared.fandom.com/wiki/West_Continent>)
- **East Continent**: Oriental-inspired, harder to access early on (only ~31 players reached it in the first three years). Ruled largely under the influence of the **Hwan Kingdom** and its yangban. Four major kingdoms share a landmass comparable to the West Continent: rich in resources and talent. Features sacred beast weapons (Blue Dragon Dao in Kaya, White Tiger Spear in Pa, Black Tortoise Jewel in Xing, Red Phoenix Bow associated with the south/Pangea). Higher overall content difficulty and power level in many areas. Access points include the Crumbling Tower and Kelenian Underwater Cave.[](<https://overgeared.fandom.com/wiki/East_Continent>)
- **Red Sea**: The dividing sea between the two continents. Major trade and travel route; Galest serves as a key gateway port.
- **Hell**: Demonic realm, harsh and dangerous. Accessed via special means (e.g., certain classes or rifts). Features places like the Hell Desert and Soul Vault.
- **Asgard / Divine realms**: Heavenly or god-related spaces. Later includes the **Overgeared World**, a mythic dimension tied to Grid and allied gods (size linked to temples in Reinhardt; grants special effects like removed cooldowns for certain deities).
- Other: Elemental World, Cultivation World (post-updates), Abyss (inter-dimensional space), Behen Archipelago (special island chain with trials and death knights of former legends), Vampire Cities (underground network), etc.

### Major Empires and Kingdoms (West Continent focus)
**Saharan Empire** (later largely integrated into Overgeared): Once the dominant power. Capital **Titan** — chosen for the continent’s only black mithril mine; imperial grandeur with palaces, legions, and economic might. **Galest** — largest port city, economic hub and Red Sea gateway. Other territories include Tiphon, Basara Duchy. Landmarks: Tower of Eternity (Goldhit’s residence, later attacked), Tower of the Sun, Abyss Dungeon (horrific political prison for high-level rebels). Borders included the Taturans Plains.[](<https://overgeared.fandom.com/wiki/Saharan_Empire>)

**Overgeared Kingdom → Overgeared Empire**: Founded by Grid after conquering Eternal. Capital shifts to **Reinhardt**, later dual capitals with Titan. Expands massively through conquest, diplomacy, and development. Includes former Eternal territories plus more.

**Eternal Kingdom** (conquered/absorbed): Northern-focused kingdom. Capital **Reinhardt** — beautiful, wealthy medieval city with hundreds of thousands of residents, 10-meter walls, protected by noble armies; spectacular architecture. Other key cities: **Patrian** (major fortress, militaristic), **Winston** (large northern city, commercial, home to Khan’s Smithy; cold climate influence nearby), **Reidan** (see detailed below), **Bairan** (smaller village that becomes a guild base), **Frontier** (Earl Steim’s capital), **Pedro** (destroyed during Golem invasion).

**Reidan** (detailed example of transformation): Originally the second-largest city in Eternal (could hold ~500,000), located in the west bordering the Saharan Empire. Surrounded by fields, rivers (Hebend River connected), lakes, and waterways. Ten years before the main story, giant worms and desertification turned the region arid; population collapsed to ~20,000 starving people, walls stretched to the horizon but were poorly maintained, security abysmal. Grid receives it as a duchy. Through farming innovations (Piaro), mining, alchemy facilities (using local yellow dust), industry, and immigration, it becomes a thriving industrial powerhouse and supply center for the empire. Nearby: Vampire Cities, Dravian Mountains, desert monsters.[](<https://overgeared.fandom.com/wiki/Reidan>)

Other notable kingdoms (many later vassalized, destroyed, or integrated):
- **Gauss Kingdom** (destroyed): Eastern areas near Elven Forest; cities like Penan.
- **Valhalla Kingdom** (successor to Belto): Borders Taturans Plains.
- **Haken Kingdom**: Eastern; cities like Yubadakan, Ellelua, Taleren (many damaged by Great Demon Berith).
- **Arc Kingdom** (sometimes Ark): Borders Volcanic Zone of Talima; fortresses (Henlutu, Kalatan, Lilchard, Peltrino), canal city on Haspachi Canal.
- **Siren Kingdom**: Aquatic themes.
- **Fold, Murray, Glaucian, Ultina, Rio, Taylor, Twilight Orc, Dominion, Dwarf Kingdom**, and others (some destroyed like Violet, Lubana, Media, Rotemon, Ul, Giant).
- Principalities: Bonkost/Bungerst (declined, Yatan activity), Burns, Hemilton (city Echiran), Luvia, Zik, etc.

### Key Cities, Castles, and Communities
- **Winston**: Bustling northern hub. Khan’s famous smithy. Castle and dungeon used in early plot (prison, corrupt lord). Parade grounds, commercial districts. Cold northern influence.
- **Bairan**: Smaller settlement near Winston; early Overgeared/Tzedakah base.
- **Patrian**: Large fortress city with strong military presence.
- **Titan** and **Galest**: Imperial centers as described above.
- East Continent examples: Pangea (southern, Red Phoenix associations), cities in Cho, Kaya, Pa, Xing, and Hwan Kingdom territories. Shangri-La (special/mythic).
- Others: Borneo (taken from Gauss), various fortresses, villages like Kent (Yatan temple), Ren Village, etc.

### Dungeons, Fields, Mountains, and Landmarks
**Dungeons**:
- **Cokro Island Dungeon**: 4 floors; Hell Gao (boss) appears every two weeks on the 4th floor.
- **Vampire Cities**: Network of 15 underground cities in the western Eternal/Overgeared region. Entrances seal after 10 seconds. Bosses are True Blood or Direct Descendant vampires (some unique and non-respawning). Require strong parties (e.g., 10+ third-advancement). Examples: 1st (Fenrir), 2nd (Marie Rose), 7th (Yetima), 8th (Latina), 9th (Cray), 10th (Tiramet), 13th (Elfin Stone, levels ~280–350). Killing bosses reduces stronger vampire spawns.[](<https://overgeared.fandom.com/wiki/Vampire_Cities>)
- **Akero Dungeon** (near Frontier), **Gerad Dungeon**, **Glacier Dungeon**, **Golem’s Labyrinth**, **Ruger Dungeon**, **Snake Dungeon**, **Vasco’s Labyrinth**, **Pangea’s Secret Dungeon**, **Abyss Dungeon** (Saharan political hellhole).
- Temples as dungeon-like: Galgunos Temple, Temple of Shadows, Yatan Church temples (e.g., Third Temple in ruined principality, Main Temple near Eight Canyon).

**Fields, Mountains, Forests, and Special Areas**:
- **Dravian Mountains**: Former nest of the dragon Nevartan; later Blood Carnival base. Near Reidan.
- **Kesan Canyon**: Steep, dangerous walls; Piaro’s hermit hideout. Site of Pagma’s Sword Dance carvings.
- **Eight Canyon**: Steep walls shaped like the number 8; Yatan Main Temple on outskirts.
- **Boundary Forest / Elven Forest / World Tree’s Forest**: Overlaps volcanic and desert zones; near Reinhardt (within ~4 days). Home to elves.
- **Beldon Volcanic Zone** and **Volcanic Zone of Talima** (surrounds Talima, dwarf-associated city); **Lilton Desert**.
- **Taturans Plains**: Border region between Saharan and Belto/Valhalla; site of major conflicts.
- **Northern snowfields**: Harsh cold, Frost Orcs, materials like sulfid scales.
- **Haalrune Swamp**, **Alzar Mountain**, **Suaz Mountains**, **Chaos Mountains**, **Grey Forest**, **Crime Forest**, **Elgad’s Forest** (ranker hunting, killer spiders/butterflies), **Thorny Vine Forest**, **Helitera Forest**, **Lamia Forest**, **Popo Forest**.
- **Behen Archipelago**: Chain of islands with progressive trials; death knights of former legends guard later islands.
- **Sword Grave**, **Ruins of the Martial God**, **Indestructible Castle**, **Tower That Grows Stronger As One Climbs It**, **Emperor’s Treasure House**, **Hexetia’s Home** (shabby cabin in a sea of clouds).
- Underwater/special: Bellitori (ancient submerged green Giant city, moss-covered ruins), Kelenian Underwater Cave, Pearl Island.
- Others: Cigna Cave, Beware Dogs dungeon area, Soul Vault (999 souls, including heroes and legends), various mines (Elliter, black mithril in Titan).

### Other Notable Mentions
Many places evolve dramatically due to player/NPC actions (especially Grid’s kingdom-building). Deserts are reclaimed, ruins rebuilt, new facilities (academies, alchemy labs, temples) appear, and political borders shift constantly. Later story expands into divine, demonic, and interdimensional spaces with their own distinct aesthetics and rules.

This covers the major and significantly described locations. The novel emphasizes living, changing geography shaped by players, NPCs, monsters, and gods rather than a static map. If you want deeper details on any specific place (e.g., full history of Reidan, Vampire Cities bosses, or East Continent kingdoms), name it and I can expand.   Build the game based on this, in 3D, in a full scale map. Implement the movement for mobile phones as well. Implement the craft system and decisions of players affecting the world. Affinity system with NPCs. Create all this in 3d, third person view.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D third-person Satisfy-inspired game based on the extensive world and mechanics description, playable with mouse/keyboard and mobile controls.
- Include a large explorable map, crafting, player-driven world decisions, and NPC affinity.

## Requirements
- User explicitly said: “Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.”
- Implement third-person 3D gameplay, mobile movement, crafting, world-changing choices, and NPC affinity.
- Make the game playable on computer and phone.

## Decisions
- Created a new Vite/Three.js game from scratch because the repository had no existing application.
- Use procedural low-poly scenery and UI rather than downloaded assets.
- Built a 560m explorable region around Winston, with broader destinations represented in a world map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `package.json` with Vite and Three.js dependencies.
- Added `index.html` with game HUD, dialogue, modal, map, and mobile control layouts.
- Added `src/style.css` with responsive desktop/mobile styling.
- Added `src/main.js` with procedural 3D terrain, town, player/NPC/enemy models, keyboard and touch movement, combat, NPC dialogue/affinity, crafting, inventory, journal, world map, decisions, and simulation HUD.

### Active
- Validate and polish the application; files have not yet been built or tested.
- Confirm `src/main.js` and `src/style.css` load and that UI/gameplay work in browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect current source files for syntax/runtime issues, especially `src/main.js`.
2. Install dependencies and run the Vite production build.
3. Launch the game and test browser rendering, movement, NPC interactions, crafting, world decisions, and mobile controls; fix discovered issues.
4. Briefly report assumptions and what is playable.

## Relevant Files
- `package.json`: Vite and Three.js dependencies and scripts.
- `index.html`: Main game UI and mobile controls.
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene and game systems.
- `src/style.css`: HUD and responsive styling.

## Important Context
- `src/main.js` was assembled in several writes/edits and has not been validated; the most recent edit added the animation loop and initialized the game.
- No dependency installation, build, browser test, or git commit has occurred.

- Build a complete, playable 3D third-person Satisfy-inspired game with exploration, crafting, world-changing choices, and NPC affinity.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Make the game playable on computer and phone.

## Decisions
- Built a new Vite/Three.js game with procedural low-poly scenery and UI.
- Created a 560m explorable region around Winston; broader destinations appear on the world map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added the game UI, responsive styles, procedural 3D world, movement, combat, NPC dialogue/affinity, crafting, inventory, journal, world map, and community decisions.
- Installed dependencies; `npm run build` succeeds with a warning that the JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB.
- Ran a Chromium smoke test: UI and canvas load, and no JavaScript exceptions were observed.

### Active
- Validate and polish gameplay and rendering; the captured Chromium screenshot showed the HUD over a flat background with no visible 3D geometry.
- Review identified a likely house placement bug: `house()` positions its group and also uses world coordinates for local meshes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Diagnose why the 3D scene is not visible in the Chromium capture; confirm whether this is a software-WebGL limitation or a rendering issue.
2. Fix any rendering or gameplay issues found, including the likely house coordinate offset.
3. Re-test build, browser rendering, interactions, and mobile layout; then summarize assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene and game systems.
- `src/style.css`: HUD and responsive styling.
- `index.html`: Game UI and controls.
- `package.json`: Scripts and dependencies.
- `package-lock.json`: Installed dependency lockfile.
- `/tmp/opencode/satisfy-game.png`: Browser screenshot showing the rendering issue.

## Important Context
- The production build completes; npm audit reported zero vulnerabilities.
- Chromium reported no JavaScript exceptions, and the canvas/WebGL context exists, but the screenshot appears to show only the scene background.
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed untracked project files including `index.html`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `src/`, and `dist/`.

## Objective
- Complete a playable 3D third-person Satisfy-inspired game with exploration, crafting, consequential choices, and NPC affinity.
- Make the game playable on computer and phone.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- Use a new Vite/Three.js game with procedural low-poly scenery and UI.
- Keep the explorable region around Winston to 560m, with farther destinations on the world map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game UI, procedural 3D world, movement, combat, NPC dialogue/affinity, crafting, inventory, journal, world map, and community decisions.
- `npm run build` previously succeeded, with a warning that the JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB.
- Browser testing confirmed the UI and WebGL canvas load without JavaScript exceptions.

### Active
- Fix rendering/gameplay: the captured scene shows only a flat background; terrain elevation likely buried the characters and scenery.
- Began adjusting `src/main.js` so terrain height is relative to the Winston spawn point; remaining object placement and browser verification are pending.
- Fix the identified house placement issue: house meshes use world coordinates inside an already-positioned group.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Finish aligning houses, trees, NPCs, player, forge, walls, bridge, and wolves to `terrainHeight` in `src/main.js`; correct house mesh coordinates to group-local positions.
2. Rebuild and capture desktop/mobile browser views to verify visible scenery, then test movement and interactions.
3. Briefly summarize assumptions and validation results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, terrain, object placement, and game systems.
- `src/style.css`: HUD and responsive styling.
- `index.html`: Game UI and controls.
- `/tmp/opencode/satisfy-game.png`: Browser screenshot showing the missing-scene issue.

## Important Context
- Current changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- The latest edit introduced `rawTerrainHeight`, `terrainOffset`, and `terrainHeight` in `src/main.js`; scene objects have not yet been aligned to the new height datum.
- A browser test at `http://127.0.0.1:5173` confirmed a canvas/WebGL context and no JavaScript exceptions, but still showed a flat background. A capture attempt against port 5173 timed out waiting for a visible body.

## Objective
- Complete a playable Satisfy-inspired 3D game with exploration, crafting, consequential choices, and NPC affinity.
- Support desktop and mobile play.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- Use a Vite/Three.js game with procedural low-poly scenery and UI.
- Keep the explorable region around Winston to 560m, with farther destinations on the world map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game UI, 3D world, movement, combat, NPC dialogue/affinity, crafting, inventory, journal, world map, and community decisions.
- Aligned scenery and characters with sampled terrain height; fixed house meshes using group-local coordinates.
- Confirmed the scene renders ground and the avatar in a screenshot.

### Active
- Recheck the latest road fix: roads now use terrain-following mesh segments with corrected upward-facing triangle winding; this change has not been captured or verified.
- Address the earlier screenshot’s oversized avatar and road visually obscuring scenery, if still present.
- Recheck desktop and mobile rendering, movement, and interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Capture the scene after the road mesh change and adjust camera/scenery visibility if needed.
2. Run `npm run build` again and check for runtime errors.
3. Test movement and interactions on desktop and mobile, then briefly summarize assumptions and validation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, terrain-following roads, camera, and game systems.
- `src/style.css`: HUD and responsive styling.
- `index.html`: Game UI and controls.
- `/tmp/opencode/after-fix.png`: Earlier screenshot showing a broad diagonal road surface and oversized avatar.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- `npm run build` succeeded before the latest road mesh edits and warned that the JS chunk exceeds 500 kB.
- The player camera distance remains unchanged; the avatar’s scale in the previous screenshot has not yet been rechecked.

## Objective
- Complete a playable Satisfy-inspired 3D game with exploration, crafting, consequential choices, and NPC affinity.
- Support desktop and mobile play.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- Use a Vite/Three.js game with procedural low-poly scenery and UI.
- Keep the explorable region around Winston to 560m, with farther destinations on the world map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game UI, 3D world, movement, combat, NPC dialogue/affinity, crafting, inventory, journal, world map, and community decisions.
- Aligned scenery and characters with sampled terrain height; fixed house meshes using group-local coordinates.
- `npm run build` succeeds; latest build warns that the JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB.

### Active
- Verify the latest terrain-following road mesh and check whether the avatar scale or road visibility needs adjustment.
- Validate desktop and mobile rendering, movement, and interactions.

### Blocked
- Browser capture did not complete: `CAPTURE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5173 CAPTURE_DIR=/tmp/opencode/capture ./capture.sh` timed out waiting for visible `body`; a separate Playwright attempt could not launch because no X server/`$DISPLAY` was set.

## Next Move
1. Resolve the browser capture setup and inspect the scene after the road mesh change.
2. Adjust camera or scenery visibility if needed.
3. Test desktop and mobile rendering, movement, and interactions; summarize assumptions and validation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, terrain-following roads, camera, and game systems.
- `src/style.css`: HUD and responsive styling.
- `index.html`: Game UI and controls.
- `/tmp/opencode/after-fix.png`: Earlier screenshot predating verification of the latest road change.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and currently untracked.
- Latest `npm run build` output: JavaScript chunk is 516.96 kB (134.66 kB gzip), above Vite’s 500 kB warning threshold.
- Latest road triangles use indices `[0,2,1,1,2,3]` to face upward; the visual result remains unverified.

## Objective
- Complete a playable Satisfy-inspired 3D game with exploration, crafting, consequential choices, and NPC affinity.
- Support desktop and mobile play.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- Use a Vite/Three.js game with procedural low-poly scenery and UI.
- Keep the explorable region around Winston to 560m, with farther destinations on the world map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game systems and aligned scenery and characters with sampled terrain height.
- `npm run build` succeeds; latest build warns that the JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB.
- Captured a fresh desktop screenshot with headless Chromium after the configured capture script timed out.

### Active
- Diagnose the desktop render: the avatar looks oversized and tan terrain/path dominates the view; check road visibility and camera framing.
- Inspect the fresh mobile screenshot and validate responsive rendering, movement, and interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/current-mobile.png` and compare against the desktop capture.
2. Diagnose and adjust camera, avatar scale, and/or road rendering based on the captures.
3. Rebuild and recheck desktop and mobile visuals and interactions; summarize assumptions and validation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, terrain-following roads, camera, and game systems.
- `src/style.css`: HUD and responsive styling.
- `index.html`: Game UI and controls.
- `/tmp/opencode/current-desktop.png`: Fresh desktop capture showing the framing/scene issue.
- `/tmp/opencode/current-mobile.png`: Fresh mobile capture awaiting inspection.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and currently untracked.
- Desktop capture command: `chromium --headless --no-sandbox --enable-webgl --enable-unsafe-swiftshader --use-gl=angle --screenshot=/tmp/opencode/current-desktop.png --window-size=1280,800 http://127.0.0.1:5173`.
- The `capture.sh` workflow timed out previously, but direct headless Chromium capture succeeded despite GPU/display warning logs.

## Objective
- Complete a playable Satisfy-inspired 3D game with exploration, crafting, consequential choices, and NPC affinity.
- Support desktop and mobile play.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- Use a Vite/Three.js game with procedural low-poly scenery and UI.
- Keep the explorable region around Winston to 560m, with farther destinations on the world map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game systems and aligned scenery and characters with sampled terrain height.
- Earlier `npm run build` succeeded, with a JavaScript chunk-size warning.
- Captured desktop and mobile screenshots; inspected both and a delayed desktop capture.
- Updated terrain fog density in `src/main.js` from `.0032` to `.0024`.

### Active
- Fix oversized avatar framing and tan terrain/path dominating desktop and mobile views.
- Improve mobile HUD space and validate responsive rendering, movement, and interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Adjust camera distance and initial position so the avatar is framed correctly from the first render.
2. Tune path width/color and lighting based on captures; review mobile HUD overlap.
3. Rebuild and recheck desktop and mobile visuals and interactions; summarize assumptions and validation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, camera, terrain, roads, and game systems.
- `src/style.css`: HUD and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/current-desktop.png`: Desktop capture showing oversized avatar and tan terrain.
- `/tmp/opencode/current-mobile.png`: Mobile capture showing oversized avatar and crowded HUD.
- `/tmp/opencode/after-wait-desktop.png`: Delayed desktop capture; framing issue persists.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and currently untracked.
- Desktop and delayed desktop captures show the avatar filling most of the view; the road is hard to distinguish from the tan terrain.
- The only change made during this continuation was lowering fog density; camera, lighting, road, and responsive HUD adjustments remain pending.

## Objective
- Complete a playable Satisfy-inspired 3D game with exploration, crafting, consequential choices, and NPC affinity.
- Support desktop and mobile play.

## Requirements
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a Vite/Three.js game with procedural low-poly scenery and UI.
- Keep the explorable region around Winston to 560m, with farther destinations on the world map.

- Latest captures show minimap labels overlapping; the CSS selectors appear inconsistent with the minimap label classes in `index.html`.
- Desktop nearby panel appears empty; mobile hides it.
- Project files remain uncommitted and untracked.

## Objective
- Complete a playable Satisfy-inspired 3D game with exploration, crafting, consequential choices, and NPC affinity.
- Support desktop and mobile play.

## Requirements
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a Vite/Three.js game with procedural low-poly scenery and UI.
- Keep the explorable region around Winston to 560m, with farther destinations on the world map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game systems and aligned scenery and characters with sampled terrain height.
- Adjusted fog, camera framing, initial camera position, path color and widths, and mobile hotbar placement.
- Fixed minimap label styling/placement to match the current HTML classes.
- Added a live, sorted nearby-NPC list for desktop; nearby entries open dialogue when in range.
- `npm run build` succeeds.

### Active
- Validate the updated minimap and nearby panel in browser captures.
- Test movement and interactions on desktop and mobile; review mobile HUD/control spacing.

### Blocked
- `capture.sh` previously failed because Playwright reported `locator('body')` hidden; direct Playwright capture worked as a workaround, but browser validation after the latest changes is still pending.

## Next Move
1. Capture and inspect the updated desktop and mobile layouts.
2. Test movement, NPC interaction, and mobile controls.
3. Summarize assumptions and validation when finished.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, movement, NPC dialogue, and nearby list.
- `src/style.css`: HUD, minimap, nearby list, and responsive styling.
- `index.html`: Game HUD structure and minimap labels.
- `/tmp/opencode/recheck/desktop.png`: Previous desktop capture, before the latest UI fixes.
- `/tmp/opencode/recheck/mobile.png`: Previous mobile capture, before the latest UI fixes.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were previously untracked.
- Build emits a warning that the minified JS chunk exceeds 500 kB.

## Objective
- Complete a playable Satisfy-inspired 3D game with exploration, crafting, consequential choices, and NPC affinity.
- Support desktop and mobile play.

## Requirements
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a Vite/Three.js game with procedural low-poly scenery and UI.
- Keep the explorable region around Winston to 560m, with farther destinations on the world map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game systems, terrain-aligned scenery and characters, minimap labels, and a sorted nearby-NPC list.
- Captured and inspected the latest desktop and mobile layouts using direct Playwright.
- `npm run build` succeeds.

### Active
- Improve and retest rendering performance: measured about 2 FPS desktop and 5 FPS mobile in the browser; latest change batches tree meshes with `THREE.InstancedMesh` and is not yet validated.
- Test movement, NPC interactions, and mobile controls after the performance change.

### Blocked
- `capture.sh` still fails waiting for `locator('body')` to become visible; direct Playwright capture works as a workaround.

## Next Move
1. Recheck desktop/mobile FPS and captures after tree instancing.
2. Test movement, interaction/dialogue choices, crafting, and mobile joystick/buttons.
3. Summarize assumptions and validation when finished.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, movement, NPC dialogue, nearby list, and recent tree-instancing change.
- `src/style.css`: HUD, minimap, nearby list, and responsive styling.
- `index.html`: Game HUD structure and minimap labels.
- `capture.sh`: Existing capture wrapper; currently fails on body visibility.
- `/tmp/opencode/recheck/desktop.png`: Latest desktop capture before tree instancing.
- `/tmp/opencode/recheck/mobile.png`: Latest mobile capture before tree instancing.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Direct Playwright captures showed a local 404 console error; its resource URL has not been identified.
- Build emits a warning that the minified JS chunk exceeds 500 kB.

## Objective
- Complete a playable Satisfy-inspired 3D game with exploration, crafting, consequential choices, and NPC affinity.
- Support desktop and mobile play.

## Requirements
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a Vite/Three.js game with procedural low-poly scenery and UI.
- Keep the explorable region around Winston to 560m, with farther destinations on the world map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game systems, terrain-aligned scenery and characters, minimap labels, and a sorted nearby-NPC list.
- Instanced tree scenery and batched road geometry to reduce draw calls.
- `npm run build` succeeded before the latest rendering and road-batching edits.

### Active
- Improve and retest rendering performance; measured 4 FPS desktop and 10 FPS mobile after lowering render resolution and disabling shadows.
- Validate the latest road batching change and retest desktop/mobile captures.
- Test movement, NPC interactions/dialogue choices, crafting, and mobile joystick/buttons.

### Blocked
- `capture.sh` still fails waiting for `locator('body')` to become visible; direct Playwright capture works as a workaround.

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build` and recheck desktop/mobile FPS and captures after the latest road batching edit.
2. Test movement, interaction/dialogue choices, crafting, and mobile controls.
3. Identify the remaining local 404 console error, then summarize assumptions and validation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, movement, NPC dialogue, nearby list, and recent rendering optimizations.
- `src/style.css`: HUD, minimap, nearby list, and responsive styling.
- `index.html`: Game HUD structure and minimap labels.
- `capture.sh`: Existing capture wrapper; currently fails on body visibility.
- `/tmp/opencode/recheck/desktop-instanced.png`: Capture before the latest performance changes.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete a playable Satisfy-inspired 3D game with exploration, crafting, consequential choices, and NPC affinity.
- Support desktop and mobile play.

## Requirements
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a Vite/Three.js game with procedural low-poly scenery and UI.
- Keep the explorable region around Winston to 560m, with farther destinations on the world map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game systems, terrain-aligned scenery and characters, minimap labels, a sorted nearby-NPC list, instanced trees, and batched roads.
- `npm run build` succeeds; latest bundle is 521.70 kB minified with a >500 kB chunk warning.
- Captured a latest desktop screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/recheck/latest/desktop.png`.

### Active
- Validate rendered performance, movement, NPC dialogue/choices, crafting, and mobile joystick/buttons.
- Identify the local resource 404; browser console showed `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)`.

### Blocked
- `capture.sh` still fails waiting for `locator('body')` to become visible; direct Playwright capture works as a workaround.
- Automated movement test did not reach Edda: after holding `s`, her distance increased from 21M to 32M and `e` did not open dialogue. Confirm control direction/movement testing.

## Next Move
1. Retest desktop/mobile FPS and captures after the road batching change; latest `npm run build` succeeded.
2. Diagnose movement/control direction, then test NPC interaction, choices, crafting, and mobile controls.
3. Identify the local 404 and summarize assumptions and validation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, movement, NPC dialogue, nearby list, and rendering optimizations.
- `src/style.css`: HUD, minimap, nearby list, and responsive styling.
- `index.html`: Game HUD structure and minimap labels.
- `capture.sh`: Existing capture wrapper; currently fails on body visibility.
- `/tmp/opencode/recheck/latest/desktop.png`: Latest desktop capture.
- `/tmp/opencode/recheck/latest/moved.png`: Capture after automated movement test.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Desktop screenshot renders the game scene and HUD; console logged one 404 resource error, but no HTTP error response was recorded.
- Prior captures are under `/tmp/opencode/recheck/`: `desktop-instanced.png`, `mobile-instanced.png`, `desktop-optimized.png`, and `mobile-optimized.png`.
- The game’s movement loop caps `dt` at `.04`; current keyboard test pressing `s` increased Edda’s distance, so movement direction/control remains unverified.

## Objective
- Complete a playable Satisfy-inspired 3D game with exploration, crafting, consequential choices, and NPC affinity.
- Support desktop and mobile play.

## Requirements
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a Vite/Three.js game with procedural low-poly scenery and UI.
- Keep the explorable region around Winston to 560m, with farther destinations on the world map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game systems, terrain-aligned scenery and characters, minimap labels, a sorted nearby-NPC list, instanced trees, and batched roads.
- `npm run build` succeeded before the latest movement-timestep edit; bundle was 521.70 kB minified with a >500 kB chunk warning.
- Confirmed the local `/favicon.ico` request returns 404.
- Confirmed pressing `w` moves toward Edda; in the prior test her displayed distance decreased from 21M to 14M.

### Active
- Validate rendered performance, NPC dialogue/choices, crafting, and mobile joystick/buttons.
- Retest movement after increasing the game-loop delta cap from `.04` to `.2` in `src/main.js`.
- Add a favicon to resolve the confirmed local 404; rebuild and verify.

### Blocked
- `capture.sh` still fails waiting for `locator('body')` to become visible; direct Playwright capture works as a workaround.
- Dialogue and crafting remain unverified: Edda was still 14M away when the interaction test ended.
- Headful Playwright test measured about 5 FPS in the current software-rendered environment; assess mobile and performance on retest.

## Next Move
1. Add a favicon so the browser no longer requests missing `/favicon.ico`.
2. Run `npm run build`, then retest movement, NPC interaction and choices, crafting, and mobile joystick/buttons.
3. Identify remaining console/network errors, capture desktop/mobile screenshots, and summarize assumptions and validation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Scene, movement, NPC dialogue, crafting, and rendering loop; latest `.2` delta cap is unverified.
- `src/style.css`: HUD and responsive/mobile styling.
- `index.html`: Game HUD and page head; favicon link belongs here.
- `capture.sh`: Existing capture wrapper; body-visibility wait has failed.
- `/tmp/opencode/recheck/latest/desktop.png`: Latest desktop capture.
- `/tmp/opencode/recheck/latest/moved.png`: Earlier capture after movement test.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- The previous `s` movement test moved away from Edda; use `w` to approach her from the spawn point.
- Local 404 is reproducible with `curl` against `http://127.0.0.1:5173/favicon.ico`.
- Latest `.2` timestep change was made after the last build and browser test.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete a playable Satisfy-inspired 3D game with exploration, crafting, consequential choices, and NPC affinity.
- Support desktop and mobile play.

## Requirements
- Support keyboard/mouse and mobile controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a Vite/Three.js game with procedural low-poly scenery and UI.
- Keep the explorable region around Winston to 560m, with farther destinations on the world map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game systems, terrain-aligned scenery and characters, minimap labels, a sorted nearby-NPC list, instanced trees, and batched roads.
- Added an SVG favicon and linked it from `index.html`; local browser test reported no failed responses.
- `npm run build` succeeds; bundle is 521.70 kB minified with a >500 kB chunk warning.
- Crafting modal and sabre crafting work; resulting inventory showed one sabre and reduced materials.

### Active
- Retest movement at a controlled duration, then verify Edda dialogue and choices.
- Verify mobile joystick movement and action buttons; controls are visible, but movement is not yet confirmed.
- Assess rendered performance and capture final screenshots.

### Blocked
- `capture.sh` previously failed waiting for `locator('body')` visibility; direct Playwright capture works.
- A 16-second movement test overshot Edda, ending 67M away; dialogue and quest choice remain unverified.
- A prior headful Playwright test measured about 5 FPS in the software-rendered environment.

## Next Move
1. Run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs` under `xvfb-run -a`; it now moves until Edda is within 9m.
2. Verify Edda dialogue/choice, mobile joystick movement, and mobile interaction; review browser errors and screenshots.
3. Summarize remaining performance concerns and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Movement, NPC dialogue, crafting, and rendering loop.
- `src/style.css`: HUD and responsive/mobile styling.
- `index.html`: Game HUD and favicon link.
- `favicon.svg`: New local favicon.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script; most recent movement adjustment is unrun.
- `/tmp/opencode/recheck/latest/desktop-final.png`: Latest desktop capture, after crafting.
- `/tmp/opencode/recheck/latest/mobile-final.png`: Latest mobile capture.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and currently untracked.
- Playwright requires `xvfb-run -a` in this environment; direct launch failed with “Missing X server or $DISPLAY”.
- `npm run build` reports a chunk-size warning for the 521.70 kB JavaScript bundle.
